newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares extend losses on NATO exclusion.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares extend losses on NATO exclusion.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 2.95 percent on Monday extending their losses to a total 6.7 percent since the United States said on Thursday they would not back Slovenia's candidacy to join NATO in 1999.

"Remaining outside of NATO means that international capital will stay away from Slovenia for a longer period than it would otherwise, therefore liquidity will remain poor and will thus push prices down," a trader said.
Analysts said the index could fall another 10 percent by the end of August as market liquidity usually dries up during the summer.
The blue-chip SBI index fell 36.44 points to 1,199.16. Overall 12 shares fell, four rose, two were unchanged and 11 were untraded. Turnover firmed to 73 million tolars from 58 million on Friday.

Petrol trader Petrol was the most actively traded, closing 0.63 percent higher at 16,100 tolars on volume of 913 shares. Traders attributed the rise to a technical rebound after Petrol fell 4.5 percent last week.
Preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the leading decliners, down 8.24 percent to 390 tolars on volume of 300 shares.
"Kovinotehna is a very illiquid share therefore even a small sell-off can push the price down significantly," an analyst said.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, up 10.75 percent to 7,930 but brokers said gains were exaggerated by the illiquidity of the share. Turnover was just 76 lots.
Petrol trader Istrabenz, which was moved to the main market from the over-the-counter (OTC) segment on Monday, eased 0.6 percent to 2,812 on volume of 107 shares.
Shopping centre operator BTC, which last week successfully finished a global depositary receipts (GDR) issue, fell six percent to 13,160 on volume of 936 shares.

"Although many believed BTC will soar following a GDR issue that did not happen. Therefore some are moving out of the share but the price is not likely to fall below 13,100 as the company is quite prosperous," a broker said.
